judged.help: Choose “together” if you are married and the two of you are filing one return, even if only one of you had income. If your husband or wife died during 2025, you can still choose “together”. If you are married but each of you files a separate return, choose “Just me”.

options.label: Me and my husband or wife, together on one return

judged.prompt: Who is this tax return for?

judged.help: Take the first line that is true for you, with one exception: if you are married but lived apart from your husband or wife for the last six months of 2025 and your child lived with you, look at the line about paying for a home before the first line. If a court decree of divorce or legal separation was final by December 31, 2025, you were not married. If you pick one of the lines about a child or relative, later questions check the details (who lived with you, for how long, who paid for the home). If they do not fit, you will be told, and you can come back and choose again.

options.label: Married, and filing apart from my husband or wife (married filing separately)
Widowed in 2023 or 2024, not remarried, and my child lived with me all of 2025 (qualifying surviving spouse)
I paid over half the cost of the home of my child, or of a relative I support (head of household)
None of these: I was not married (single)
Married, and filing together with my husband or wife on one return (married filing jointly)

judged.prompt: Which of these fits you on December 31, 2025?

judged.help: Yes if you or your spouse were a nonresident alien for any part of 2025, or you have any income or return treatment the question names, or any other outside the wages, interest, dividends, securities sales, Form 1099-R distributions and social security benefits this tool handles; Yes refuses the return.
judged.prompt:
Any nonresident alien status, or other income or return treatment outside the kinds listed below?

Kinds this question is not about:
- wages
- interest
- dividends
- supported securities sales
- Form 1099-R distributions
- social security benefits

Nonresident alien status:
- you or your spouse, for any part of 2025

Other income or return treatment, including:
- wages or tips not on a Form W-2
- Medicaid waiver payments (whether or not in Form W-2 box 1)
- adoption benefits
- dependent care benefits other than those shown in box 10 of a Form W-2 (or a grace-period amount from such a plan)
- other earned income (Form 1040 lines 1b to 1d and 1f to 1h)
- income or loss from a passive activity (including gain on selling an interest in one)
- the 2025 part of a qualified disaster recovery distribution you received in 2023 or 2024, or a 2025 repayment of one (Form 8915-F)
- a repayment to an IRA of a qualified reservist distribution (Form 8606 line 1)
- you or your spouse being a debtor in a chapter 11 bankruptcy case open at any time in 2025, even if your only income is wages, interest or dividends

scope.other_income.note:
This question groups together a bunch of unrelated concepts that do not belong together:
1. non-resident alien status
2. hodgepodge of unsupported income varieties

it would be better to ask each of these individually, e.g.

"Did you receive adoption benefits?"
"Did you receive income or loss from a passive activity?" (this one needs a gloss)

etc.

This question by itself covers such a massive and detailed array of stuff
